## 1 · The trigger 🌅
7am daily: Open-Meteo for cloud, wind, rain and the sunset time; Google Calendar free/busy for both of you after six.

parameters.content:
## 2 · The hunt 🔎
Her saved spots → Google Places for the details → Claude picks the window-on-sunset table → a browser agent CHECKS the booking page. Nothing is booked yet.

parameters.text: =🍝 She picked leftovers on the couch. Nothing was booked. Netflix it is.

parameters.content:
## 3 · The pitch 💌
To HER Telegram: everything except the restaurant's name. Only the yes button carries on.

parameters.message: ={{ 'Hi ' + $('Romeo settings').first().json.BABYSITTER.name + '! Any chance you can babysit ' + $('Write the invite').first().json.day + ', from ' + $('Write the invite').first().json.niceTime + ' til about 10? $' + $('Romeo settings').first().json.BABYSITTER.ratePerHour + '/hr as usual 🙏' }}

additionalFields.description: Dress code: {{ $('Book the table').first().json.dressCode }}. Where? Surprise.

parameters.content:
## 4 · The cascade 🌹
Only after yes: the agent books the table with the candle note in the special requests, the babysitter gets a yes/no, the closest florist to her work gets the order, and the night goes in both calendars.

## 5 · The drive home 🏠
Its own trigger. An iPhone Shortcut posts your location every few minutes after dinner (Apple has no Find My API). Inside ten minutes of home, once: Wise pays the babysitter, Home Assistant turns the heater on, Spotify plays her song.

## 6 · Her saves 📌
Instagram has no API for saved posts. So she (or you) forwards a post to the bot: Romeo reads it, and if it's a restaurant, files it for the next perfect sunset.
